name: The Crucible — machine replication ledger
description: Scientific and technical claims rebuilt as minimal computational models and tested. REPRODUCED = the mechanism holds in a minimal model; FAILED = it does not; NOT_COMPUTABLE = no simulable core (an honest pass).

entries.claim: In DiD with FEW treated units and spatially/serially-correlated errors, standard DiD inference under-covers (invalid CIs) while synthetic control is materially better when parallel trends ~holds
entries.source: Alvarez & Ferman (2020)
entries.note: N=30,T=12,1 treated,rho=0.7,true effect=0,800 reps: DiD 95% CI coverage=0.305 (severe under-coverage vs nominal 0.95); SC coverage=0.891; SC RMSE=1.017 < DiD RMSE=1.267. DiD inference invalid, SC materially better.

entries.claim: Context-aware AI augmentation (adaptive type/timing/scale) preserves cognitive flow (difficulty-skill match); poorly-timed/scaled interventions disrupt flow and hurt reasoning performance
entries.source: Dissanayake & Nanayakkara (2025)
entries.note: Design/HCI framework, not a falsifiable empirical claim: a minimal flow model (flow=difficulty-skill match) confirms a gap-closing intervention by construction, so the directional result is near-tautological — no genuine FAILED was possible. Downgraded from a constructed-model REPRODUCED to keep the ledger honest.

entries.claim: Removing top-10% degree nodes from a BA network (N=2000,m=2) raises the bond-percolation threshold p_c 0.174->0.776
entries.source: Simultaneous Degradation of Percolation and Cascade
entries.note: Mechanism+direction reproduced: hub removal collapses <k^2> 50.8->3.8, p_c jumps ~8x (0.085->0.687 via Cohen mean-field). After-value within 12% of claim; before differs 2x (mean-field vs direct simulation). Robust-yet-fragile confirmed.

entries.claim: Derenyi-Palla-Vicsek (2005): k-clique percolation in ER graphs at p_c(k)=[(k-1)N]^(-1/(k-1)); for k=3, p_c ~ 1/sqrt(2N)
entries.source: Clique Percolation in Random Networks (Derenyi, Palla, Vicsek, 2005)
entries.note: k=3 scaling exponent confirmed: empirical p_c*sqrt(2N) constant across N=400/800/1600 (1.26,1.26,1.19). N^(-1/2) scaling reproduced; prefactor ~1.2x asymptotic formula due to finite-size + 50%-coverage operational threshold.

entries.claim: Berger (2003): conditional-frequentist testing reconciles Fisher/Neyman/Jeffreys - the conditional error probability equals the Bayesian posterior; the naive p-value overstates evidence against H0
entries.source: Berger (2003), Could Fisher, Jeffreys and Neyman Have Agreed on Testing?
entries.note: Calibration exact: empirical freq(H0 true | evidence) = Bayesian P(H0|x) across all bins. Berger-Sellke: p=0.05 -> P(H0|x)=0.216, p=0.005 -> 0.041 (p-value overstates evidence ~4x at 0.05).

entries.claim: Systems in the same universality class share the same critical exponents (Lubeck 2004)
entries.source: Universal Scaling Behavior of Non-Equilibrium Phase Transitions (Sven Lubeck, 2004)
entries.note: Three structurally different Z2 mean-field models (tanh self-consistency, phi^4 free energy, arctan self-consistency) all give order-parameter exponent beta=0.500; a different-class absorbing-state model gives beta=1.000. Same class -> same

entries.claim: LinUCB (Chu et al 2011): linear contextual bandit achieves O(sqrt(Td log^3)) i.e. sublinear ~sqrt(T) regret w.p. 1-delta
entries.source: Contextual Bandits with Linear Payoff Functions (Chu, Li, Reyzin, Schapire, 2011)
entries.note: Empirical regret growth exponent 0.03-0.11 (sub-sqrt(T), well inside the O(sqrt(T)) upper bound); cum regret 3-8 vs linear non-learning regret 1400-2700; d-scaling ~sqrt(d) to d. Computable core holds.

entries.claim: BA(N=2000,m=2): removing top-10% nodes by degree raises bond-percolation threshold p_c 0.174 -> 0.776 (~4.5x)
entries.source: Simultaneous Degradation of Percolation and Cascade Robustness Under Targeted Hub Removal (Cachero Sanchez, 2026-03-05)
entries.note: MC before/after = 0.150/0.680 (ratio 4.53x) vs claimed ratio 4.46x; absolute values within finite-size tolerance. Cascade claim at phi=0.22 out of scope.

entries.note: A null model with ZERO metacognitive deficit (identical self-error at every skill level) reproduces the canonical plot AND its asymmetry: bottom +45.8 (DK: +46), top -14.2 (DK: -13) - just regression to the mean on a noisy test + a UNIFORM

entries.claim: Social media platforms enable rapid dissemination of information but also facilitate the spread of misinformation
entries.source: internal corp finding (descriptive)
entries.note: Descriptive trend claim with no stated mechanism or quantity; the simulable core (false-news cascades spread farther/faster, Vosoughi 2018) is a DIFFERENT, specific claim - queued as a future Crucible target rather than strawmanned here.

entries.claim: Gilovich, Vallone & Tversky (1985): the basketball hot hand is a cognitive illusion - P(hit | streak of hits) is no higher than P(hit | streak of misses), so streak shooting does not exist
entries.source: Gilovich, Vallone & Tversky, Cognitive Psychology 17, 1985 - The hot hand in basketball: On the misperception of random sequences
entries.note: The canonical method manufactures its own conclusion. An iid shooter with NO hot hand shows P(hit|3H)-P(hit|3M) = -7.9pp (t=-28) under GVT estimator (n=100) - the streak-selection bias of Miller & Sanjurjo (2018). Bias grows to -17pp at k=4

entries.claim: Hong-Page (2004): a randomly selected (diverse) team of problem solvers outperforms the team of individually best solvers under relay search (n=2000, l=12, k=3, group 10)
entries.source: Hong & Page, PNAS 101(46), 2004 - Groups of diverse problem solvers can outperform groups of high-ability problem solvers
entries.note: Reproduced at paper params: random beats best by +1.65 (t=4.1). But the effect is FRAGILE, as critics argued: it shrinks with a narrower heuristic pool (l=6: +0.90) and REVERSES on smoothed landscapes (-0.38, ability wins) - diversity trump

entries.claim: In scale-free networks the epidemic threshold vanishes as N grows (lambda_c = <k>/<k^2> -> 0 via the <k^2> divergence), unlike homogeneous networks which keep a finite threshold.
entries.source: Epidemic spreading in scale-free networks (Pastor-Satorras & Vespignani, 2001)
entries.note: Smallest model: heterogeneous mean-field SIS threshold lambda_c=<k>/<k^2>, BA (scale-free) vs ER (homogeneous) at mean degree ~4. BA <k^2> grows with N (45->63 over N=500->20000) so lambda_c shrinks 0.088->0.064, heading to 0 = threshold VA
